input.strategy_title: GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Platform teams fund shared GPU clusters but cannot attribute consumption to the
projects using them, so capacity costs are socialized and heavy users have no
incentive to release resources. The in-flight metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is delivering per-project GPU-hour usage data; this strategy
builds the administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of that data. The
metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until that
strategy lands — reporting work here consumes it, and must not re-implement
collection.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API for finance tooling. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- The metering collection pipeline itself (RHAISTRAT-9990)
- Currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars

## Open Questions

1. The metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report
   implementation consuming it carries that external timing risk.

# Validate metering data schema against chargeback reporting needs

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's open question: the per-project
GPU-hour usage data schema owned by the in-flight GPU usage metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is not final until that strategy lands, and the chargeback
reporting built in this strategy consumes it. The investigation confirms what
the landed schema provides, validates that it supports every chargeback
reporting need, and produces a written consumption mapping plus a gap report
that can be fed back to the metering strategy while it can still change.

## Scope

- Review the metering data schema as designed/delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990
  (per-project GPU-hour usage data), tracking it to finalization.
- Produce a consumption mapping from the schema's elements to the chargeback
  reporting needs: per-project attribution, selectable time-range aggregation,
  current-month rollup, and export/API retrieval.
- Evaluate each reporting requirement against the schema and mark it supported
  or gap-identified, with a proposed schema remediation for each gap.
- Deliver the gap report to the metering strategy owners so gaps can be
  addressed before that strategy lands.
- Recommend whether the reporting implementation can proceed on the current
  schema or must wait for remediation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written consumption mapping exists that maps each relevant metering schema
  element to the chargeback reporting needs (per-project attribution,
  selectable time ranges, current-month rollup).
- Every reporting requirement (per-project GPU-hour reports, time-range
  selection, current-month consumption vs Kueue quota comparison, CSV export,
  API retrieval) is evaluated against the schema and marked either supported
  or gap-identified, and each identified gap carries a proposed remediation.
- A gap report is delivered to the metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) owners.
- A go/no-go recommendation documents whether the reporting implementation can
  proceed on the current schema or must wait for remediation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the schema validation confirms the data foundation for
  per-project GPU-hour consumption reports; gates the report computation and
  the administrator views.
- HLR-2 (P1): export/API retrieval requirements are among the needs validated
  against the schema.
- HLR-3 (P1): current-month rollup and quota-comparison data needs are among
  the needs validated against the schema.

## Risks / Notes

- The metering schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; this
  investigation's completion is therefore exposed to that strategy's timing.
  Early validation of the draft design is the mitigation — gaps found now can
  still be fixed upstream.

# Per-project GPU-hour report computation, CSV export and stable API

## Description

This epic delivers the reporting backend for GPU chargeback: computation of
per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges from the
metering data delivered by the GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990),
CSV export of those reports, and a stable API through which finance tooling
can retrieve them. It consumes the metering data as delivered and does not
re-implement usage collection (explicitly out of scope for this strategy).

## Scope

- Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over
  administrator-selectable time ranges from the metering data.
- Provide CSV export of the reports.
- Provide a stable API for retrieving reports, suitable for finance tooling
  integration.
- Consume the metering data exactly as delivered by the metering strategy —
  no duplication of the collection pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given metered per-project GPU-hour usage data, the computed report for a
  selected time range matches the aggregated GPU-hours per project for that
  range.
- Reports are exportable as CSV.
- Reports are retrievable via a stable API usable by finance tooling.
- The computation consumes the metering data as delivered by the metering
  strategy and contains no usage-collection logic (out-of-scope guard).
- The report computation is validated against the confirmed metering data
  schema before integration (gated by the schema validation outcome; if the
  landed schema differs from the reporting assumptions, the consumption
  mapping is re-derived before this epic's approach is finalized).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges, computed from the metering data — the computation half of this HLR
  (the administrator-facing viewing half is delivered by the Dashboard work).
- HLR-2 (P1, bundled): CSV export and stable API retrieval — delivery modes
  of the same report data the P0 computation produces; they share the report
  data structure and API surface, so they are not separately schedulable and
  stay bundled with the HLR-1 computation.

## Risks / Notes

- External timing risk: the metering data schema finalizes only when
  RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; this epic starts only after the schema validation
  confirms the data foundation.
- Reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars — currency/cost-rate modelling is out
  of scope.

# Dashboard administrator chargeback reporting views

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator-facing chargeback reporting experience in
the Dashboard: platform administrators can view per-project GPU-hour
consumption reports over selectable time ranges, and see current-month
consumption against each project's Kueue quota. The Dashboard presents report
data computed by the reporting backend — it does not recompute consumption
(the Dashboard owns no data plane) — and reads Kueue quota from the platform's
existing queueing CRs.

## Scope

- Administrator view of per-project GPU-hour consumption reports with
  selectable time ranges, surfacing the report data provided by the reporting
  backend delivered under this strategy.
- Administrator view showing current-month consumption against each project's
  Kueue quota.
- Restrict the chargeback reporting views to platform administrators.
- Consume report data from the reporting capability — no re-aggregation or
  recomputation of GPU-hours in the Dashboard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports for a
  selectable time range, with figures matching the reporting backend's output
  for that range.
- An administrator can see current-month consumption shown against each
  project's Kueue quota.
- Consumption figures displayed in the Dashboard are surfaced from the
  reporting backend without recomputation in the Dashboard.
- The chargeback reporting views are visible only to platform administrators.
- The views are validated against the confirmed metering data schema
  dimensions (gated by the schema validation outcome; if the available data
  dimensions differ, the view scope is re-derived).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption
  reports over selectable time ranges — the viewing half of this HLR (the
  computation half is delivered by the reporting backend work).
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the current-month consumption-vs-Kueue-quota view is
  presented in the same administrator view surface over the same report data
  as the HLR-1 viewing; it is not separately schedulable and stays bundled.

## Risks / Notes

- Depends on the reporting backend's report data surface being available;
  the Dashboard builds against it (the Dashboard owns no data plane and
  speaks the Kubernetes API per its architecture context).

# Chargeback reporting documentation (report semantics and export integration)

## Description

This epic documents GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators and
finance tooling integrators: what the reports mean — including what counts as
a GPU-hour — and how to integrate with the CSV export and the stable report
API. It follows the Red Hat docs content process and is authored after the
reporting implementation is complete so the content describes what was
actually built.

## Scope

- Documentation topic(s) covering report semantics: what the per-project
  GPU-hour consumption reports measure, what counts as a GPU-hour, time-range
  selection, and current-month consumption vs Kueue quota.
- Documentation covering export integration: CSV export usage and retrieval
  via the stable API for finance tooling.
- Content outline:
  - Report semantics: GPU-hour definition, per-project attribution, time
    ranges, quota comparison.
  - Export integration: CSV export, stable API retrieval, finance-tooling
    integration guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers report semantics, including an explicit
  definition of what counts as a GPU-hour.
- Published documentation covers export integration (CSV export and stable
  API retrieval) for finance tooling.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented chargeback
  reporting capability (report computation, export, API, and administrator
  views) and any discrepancies found in review are resolved.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a
  GPU-hour) and export integration.

## Risks / Notes

- Priority P1 is derived from the strategy frontmatter priority (Major), per
  the docs-authoring priority exception; this epic does not push priority
  onto the implementations it depends on.
- Documentation must not describe currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are
  in GPU-hours only (out of scope for the strategy).
